verdict.rationale: Stripe's machine payments docs set out stablecoin rails for agent payments. Agents pay in USDC via MPP on Tempo and Solana or via x402 on Base. The on-chain settlement is recorded as a PaymentIntent, lands in the Stripe balance and settles in fiat. The open MPP spec and the mppx SDK are publicly published, and `mppx validate` verifies an implementation end-to-end. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of a stablecoin settlement, availability beyond US states other than New York, stablecoin support in the Agentic Commerce Suite checkout flows (it is documented only for machine payments), and fuller end-to-end documentation (a community report calls the MPP docs sparse).

support.subject: As a developer, I can settle agent-initiated payments in stablecoins over documented rails

citations.quote: Stablecoin payments are available to businesses in all US states, except New York.
Payments land directly in your Stripe balance and settle in fiat. Metrics, reporting, and multi-currency payouts work the same as any other payment in Stripe
After the facilitator settles the payment on-chain, Stripe records it as a [PaymentIntent]
your server returns an HTTP 402 response with payment details, including a Stripe deposit address.
Your server returns a payment challenge, the agent presents a valid payment credential, and Stripe settles the payment to your Stripe balance.
